dedupe_keys.name: flood conditioned traction power dependency of london s rail transit under climate change

description: This study is presented by its authors as the first quantitative assessment of how flood-induced failures of traction power substations propagate through an urban rail transit system. Wei Bi, Bryan T. Adey and Jürgen Hackl built a double-layer network of London's rail transit services and their power supply, overlaid surface water flood exposure, simulated service disruption, and defined a flood-conditioned power dependency index plus a journey-based performance metric that captures robustness and redundancy. Scenarios combine current and RCP8.5 climate, two traction power feeding mechanisms (single-end and double-end) and four substation flood-failure thresholds. With double-end feeding the performance loss attributable to power is minimal; single-end feeding causes much larger loss and is very sensitive to the failure threshold, and the index correlates strongly with dependency-related loss, so it can stand in for cascading consequences in strategic planning. Coverage: the London rail transit network. Access: arXiv preprint of September 2026. Licence and cost: CC BY 4.0, free. Caveats: a preprint, the substation-to-line mapping and failure thresholds are modelling assumptions, and no dataset is released with it. It informs cascading failure, resilience and climate adaptation studies of transit power supply, and relates to the TfL Unified API record for network and service data.

name: Flood-conditioned traction power dependency of London's rail transit under climate change
outcomes: Traction power redundancy decides how far floods cascade: with double-end feeding the power-attributable loss is minimal, with single-end feeding it is much larger and sensitive to the substation failure threshold; the proposed dependency index tracks that loss closely.
